question: what the original does with guiButtonType/checkboxType `parent`, guiButtonType `scale`, scrollbarType `priority`, iconType `buttonMesh`, and listboxType `step`, `priority` and `allwaystransparent`
slots_noted: Every function here sits in a no-RTTI gui table (GuiType_guiButtonType 0x1206AD0, GuiType_scrollbarType 0x1206958, GuiType_listboxType 0x1206A64, GuiType_iconType 0x12021B0, GuiObject_guiButtonType 0x1207698) whose slot is given in the comment, except ReturnFloatOne (0x65F480): a folded `fld1; ret` held by ten dwords of .rdata, one of them CEU3Minimap slot 64 (the default GetScale inherited from CIcon/CGuiObject), so it is recorded class-free and no class gets the slot.

Two jump tables, tokens 0x2E..0xBF (byte table VA 0xB2D39C, jump table 0xB2D354) and 0x141..0x17E (0xB2D44C, 0xB2D430), and `upsound` (0x140) tested alone; key to offset: `borderSize` +0x294 ({x y}), `upSprite` +0x78, `downSprite` +0x94, `overSprite` +0xCC, `dissableSprite` +0xE8, **`spriteType` and `quadTextureSprite` both +0x104**, `position` +0x254 ({x y}), **`scale` +0x290 and `rotation` +0x28C, both floats through ParseFloat (0x67B640)**, **`parent` +0x13C** (ParseString), `tooltip` +0x120, `tooltipText` +0x21C, `delayedTooltipText` +0x238, `buttonText` +0x200, **`buttonFont` and `origo` both +0xB0**, `orientation` +0x25C, **`size` +0x280** ({x y}), **`format` +0x288** (tokens 0x74 centre 2, 0x73 right 1, 0x72 left 0), `oversound` +0x158, `clicksound` +0x174, `downsound` +0x190, `upsound` +0x1AC (token 0x140), `shortcut` +0x1E4, `luaClick` +0x1C8; everything else goes to CGuiType::LoadKey (0xAC8710). addresses.name: GuiType_guiButtonType::ResolveParent
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 of GuiType_guiButtonType (0x1206AD0): what `parent` does - inheritance from another declaration by name.** `typeTree` is the gui-type tree of the declaration's container (a windowType's +0x150, a scrollbarType's +0x160, the CGui's +0x34 for a top-level one), whose slot 1 is GuiTypeTree_FindByString - case-insensitive, null where absent. The declaration's list of inheritable keys (vector +0x68/+0x6C, filled by GuiType_guiButtonType_Construct) is **quadTextureSprite (the +0x104 sprite, so `spriteType` too), parent, tooltipText, position and delayedTooltipText**. (1) If every key on the list is set (GuiType_guiButtonType_IsKeySet), or `parent` is empty, nothing happens. (2) Otherwise P = tree.Find(parent) - **no null test, so a parent the container does not hold reads through a null pointer** - and every unset key is copied from P (GuiType_guiButtonType_SetKey). (3) If keys are still unset and P's own parent is non-empty and differs from this declaration's name, P becomes tree.Find(P.parent) and (2) repeats - a chain walked to its end; only a loop straight back to this declaration is caught. (4) When the chain ends with keys still unset: `tooltipText` becomes `Please add Text` and `delayedTooltipText` `Please add Text To the delayTooltip` (a `tooltip` branch setting `NOTOOLTIP` exists but `tooltip` is not on the list, so it never runs). Last, in every case, +0x278 = ParseGuiOrientation(+0x25C). **`position` is on the list and has a copy case but IsKeySet answers set for it always, so position is never inherited.** Children are visited in the tree's order (alphabetical, case-insensitive) by TernarySearchTree_ForEach from the container's own slot 7. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guikeys.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0xB2C6E0-0xB2CD9C (`ret 4`; retsBefore finds no earlier ret): the three loops over +0x68..+0x6C calling 0xB2D4D0, the copy switch (byte table 0xB2CDD4, jump table 0xB2CDA0) whose twelve cases each hand SetKey the parent's field at the token's own offset, the two string compares at 0xB2CA18 and 0xB2CAC6 that decide whether to climb, and the three placeholder strings at 0x15FF8C0, 0x1606A9C and 0x1606AAC. The list's five tokens read off the constructor at VA 0xB2DCC9-0xB2DD34. Wrong if slot 7 were not called after loading: CWindowType's slot 7 (0xAC5350) and GuiType_scrollbarType's (0xB287E0) each walk their own tree with the thunk 0xA7E200 (`jmp [vt+0x1C]`) passing that tree, and CGui::ResolveTypeParents does the same for the CGui's.

addresses.name: TernarySearchTree_ForEach
addresses.signature: void __stdcall TernarySearchTree_ForEach(void* node@stack:4, void* callback@stack:8, void* context@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment: Walks a ternary search tree (node layout as TernarySearchTreeFind's) in order: the low child (+8), the node's value (+0) - `callback` called with ECX = the value and `context` pushed - then the equal child (+0x10), then the high child (+0xC). So the values come in the keys' order, case-insensitive as the tree is built. ECX is handed on unchanged to the recursive calls. `ret 0xC`. The name is ours.

It clears uses_entry_heights (+0x13E), entry_count (+0x144) and the hidden-entries list (+0x128), keeps its declaration at +0x140 (its eleventh argument, [ebp+0x30]), makes the scrollbar the declaration names when it names one (+0xF8) and hides it, and leaves its own scrollbar observer at +0x100. **Where there is a scrollbar it is placed at x = the box's width (+0xDC, a short) + the declaration's `offset` x (+0xFC), y = `offset` y (+0x100)** - the scrollbar's +0x74 and +0x78, as floats (VA 0xA8C28F..0xA8C2F1); with no `offset` that is the box's right edge at its top. **`allwaystransparent` is read here and nowhere else** (VA 0xA8C43E-0xA8C476): where the declaration's +0x198 is 0, the box's drawn object (+0xB4) is registered with the box in the graphics' list at +0xD8 (0xA78360) - the same registration GuiButton_Construct makes for a button's picture, CIcon's constructor for an icon's and the CFixedWindow constructor for a window's background; `allwaystransparent = yes` skips it, so the box's own background is not one of the pictures the mouse is resolved against. Thirteen stack arguments. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-listbox.md, section 5, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guikeys.md, section 5.

addresses.comment: **The `iconType` grammar of a .gui file**, slot 4 of GuiType_iconType (0x12021B0). `ret 8`. Seven keys of its own, the rest to CGuiType::LoadKey (0xAC8710): **`spriteType` (0x35) and `buttonMesh` (0xA9) share one case body - ParseString into +0x6C** - so `buttonMesh` is a second spelling of `spriteType` and the later of the two in a block wins; `position` (0x4B) +0x94 through ParseIntPairXY, setting the byte +0x9C to 1; `3dposition` (0xAC) +0x88 through ParseVector3, setting +0x9C to 0; `scale` (0x5C) +0xA0 through ParseFloat; `orientation` (0xBF) +0xA4 as ParseGuiOrientation of the text; `frame` (0x123) +0xA8 by sscanf `%i`; `rotation` (0x17E) +0xAC by sscanf `%f`. An iconType has no `parent`: the token falls to CGuiType::LoadKey and slot 7 is the folded `ret 4` (0x20CD50). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guikeys.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0xAC8320-0xAC84CC: the jump table for 0x35..0xA9 (byte table 0xAC84E0, jump table 0xAC84D0) sends 0x35 and 0xA9 to the same body at 0xAC836D (`add esi, 0x6C; push esi; call 0xA7AFB0`), 0x4B to 0xAC838D and 0x5C to 0xAC83B4; 0xAC tested alone, 0xBF, 0x123 and 0x17E by the subtract chain at 0xAC83FB. Tokens named from ghidra/saveTokens.json. Wrong if the byte table sent 0xA9 elsewhere - read from the image, index 0x74.

struct_fields.name: inherited_keys_begin

struct_fields.evidence: `lea edi, [esi+0x68]` and the five vector inserts at VA 0xB2DCC9-0xB2DD34; ResolveParent walks [ebx+0x68]..[ebx+0x6C] at 0xB2C738.

struct_fields.name: inherited_keys_end
struct_fields.comment: End of the inheritable-key vector at +0x68.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp esi, [ebx+0x6C]` at VA 0xB2C749.

struct_fields.name: sprite
struct_fields.comment: `spriteType` or `quadTextureSprite` (one field for both). Inherited from `parent` when empty.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2CF63 for tokens 0x35 and 0x81; IsKeySet's 0x81 case at 0xB2D64F.

struct_fields.name: parent
struct_fields.comment: `parent = name`: the name of a declaration in the same container whose sprite, tooltipText and delayedTooltipText fill this one's empty ones (ResolveParent). Every widget constructor that is handed it (GuiButton_Construct, CheckBox_Construct, 0xB41570, 0xB5AA00) only destroys it.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2CFCC (token 0x84); GetParentName copies it; GuiButton_Construct's by-value copy at [ebp+0x20] is touched only by the free at 0xB40603-0xB4061F, CheckBox_Construct's only at 0xA817E0-0xA817FC.

struct_fields.name: tooltip_text
struct_fields.comment: `tooltipText`. Inherited from `parent` when empty; where a parent chain ends with it still empty it becomes `Please add Text`.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2D016 (token 0x90); the placeholder from 0x1606A9C through SetKey at 0xB2CCD6.

struct_fields.name: delayed_tooltip_text
struct_fields.comment: `delayedTooltipText`. Inherited from `parent` when empty; where a parent chain ends with it still empty it becomes `Please add Text To the delayTooltip`.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2D03B (token 0x91); the placeholder from 0x1606AAC through SetKey at 0xB2CD31.

struct_fields.name: rotation
struct_fields.comment: `rotation`, 0.0 by default; GuiButton_Construct stores it at the widget's +0x14C and gives it to the drawn object's slot 34 (CSprite::SetRotation).
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2D310 through ParseFloat; `fld [edi+0x28C]` in the create at 0xB2C14A.

struct_fields.name: scale
struct_fields.comment: `scale`, 1.0 by default; handed to GuiButton_Construct (widget +0x150) by the guiButtonType create (slot 11) only. The checkboxType create (slot 12, 0xB2BEE0) does not read it, so a checkboxType's `scale` does nothing.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB2CFAA through ParseFloat; the constructor's 1.0 at 0xB2DCB2; the create's `fld [edi+0x290]` at 0xB2C124. A byte-search scan of every [reg+0x290] in .text finds, in the gui types' code (VA 0xB28000-0xB30000), only those three; the other hits are in other classes (CFixedWindow's own +0x290 at 0xABFAD8 among them). Positive control: the same scan finds the create's read.

struct_fields.name: rotation
struct_fields.comment: The declaration's `rotation`; given to the drawn object's slot 34 when the button is built.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from GuiButton_Construct's argument at [ebp+0xD0] at VA 0xB3FBA7, read at 0xB40014 and passed to the drawn object's slot 34 (+0x88).

struct_fields.name: scale
struct_fields.comment: The declaration's `scale`. Read only by slot 64 (ReturnFloatAt150), which only GuiButton_SetDisplayObject (slot 56) calls, to give a new drawn object its C2dObject::SetScale: the picture made at construction keeps 1.0.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from [ebp+0xD8] at VA 0xB3FBE3; every float load of [reg+0x150] in .text listed by byte search and none is in the button's code but 0xB56050; the one float-consuming dispatch through +0x100 is at 0xB40A84.

struct_fields.name: parent
struct_fields.comment: The scrollbarType's own `parent`, for its own inheritance (GuiType_scrollbarType::ResolveParent). The create hands its address to CScrollbar_Construct, which was not followed for it.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB28C7E (token 0x84); ResolveParent's empty test at 0xB28855; `lea edx, [esi+0x110]` in the create at 0xB2851E.

struct_fields.name: priority
struct_fields.comment: `priority`, 0.0 by default, inheritable from `parent`. **Read by nothing else**: not by the create (0xB284C0), not by CScrollbar_Construct, not by the live scrollbar.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey's case at VA 0xB28D50 through ParseFloat; default at 0xB28286. Every [reg+0x154] in .text listed by byte search: in the scrollbar type's code only the constructor, LoadKey, ResolveParent (0xB28957), IsKeySet (0xB297B1) and SetKey (0xB299C4). Positive control: the same scan finds the create's read of startValue, [esi+0x150] at 0xB2855C. Wrong if something copied the declaration whole - nothing in the create does.

struct_fields.name: inherited_keys_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of the vector of save tokens the scrollbar may inherit from its `parent` (thirteen, priority among them), filled by its constructor.
struct_fields.evidence: The thirteen inserts at VA 0xB2830C-0xB28427; ResolveParent walks [edi+0x188]..[edi+0x18C] at 0xB288A0.

struct_fields.name: parent
struct_fields.comment: The listboxType's `parent`, for its own inheritance (GuiType_listboxType::ResolveParent). The create hands its address to GuiListBoxBase_Construct beside the background's (+0xA0); what that does with it was not read.
struct_fields.evidence: ResolveParent's `lea esi, [edi+0x84]` and empty test at VA 0xB2B2C5; LoadKey's token 0x84 case per its record; `lea edx, [esi+0x84]` pushed at 0xB2BE69.

struct_fields.name: priority
struct_fields.comment: `priority` (ParseFloat). Read only by the type's IsKeySet and SetKey, and not even inherited, since it is not on the inheritable list: **a list box's priority does nothing**.
struct_fields.evidence: Every [reg+0x114] in VA 0xB2A000-0xB2C000 and in the list box widget's code (0xA8B000-0xA8F800): LoadKey 0xB2B6A8, ResolveParent 0xB2B37A, IsKeySet 0xB2B9DD, SetKey 0xB2BC69; and every `mov r, [x+0x140]` in .text followed by a read through r of +0x114 - none (positive control: the same scan finds +0xFC/+0x100 at 0xA8C29E/0xA8C2A4 and +0x198 at 0xA8C44B).

struct_fields.name: inherited_keys_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of the vector of save tokens the list box may inherit from its `parent`: size, position, background, step, borderSize, orientation.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea edi, [esi+0x144]` at VA 0xB2B157 and the six inserts at 0xB2B1B0-0xB2B234.

struct_fields.name: step
struct_fields.comment: `step` and `spacing` (ParseInt), 1 by default. **Read by nothing**: not by the create, not by the widget, and its inheritance case is missing.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov dword [esi+0x158], 1` at VA 0xB2B165, LoadKey 0xB2B726. Every [reg+0x158] in the type's code and the widget's, and every read through a widget's +0x140: none but those two (the widget's own byte +0x158, set to 1 at 0xB2BE9D and read by its slots 4 and 6, is a different field). Same positive control as priority.

struct_fields.name: always_transparent
struct_fields.comment: `allwaystransparent` (ParseBool), no by default. Read once, by GuiListBoxBase_Construct through the widget's +0x140: where it is no the box's drawn object is registered in the graphics' +0xD8 list, as every button, icon and window background is; where yes it is not.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov byte [esi+0x198], al` at VA 0xB2B19D; `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x198], 0; jne 0xA8C47B` at 0xA8C44B skipping the push_back 0xA78360 at 0xA8C476.
